chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hussein, linking it up through his chain to God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), that he said:
Three people whom the Honorable, the Exalted God will not protect: a man who resides in a ruined house; a man who prays on the roadside; and a man who leaves his mount unsecured.
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people that God will not protect according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights three specific negligence scenarios—dwelling in ruins, praying on thoroughfares, and leaving mounts unsecured—where God's protective care (al-hifz) is withheld due to a lack of proper stewardship. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *tadbir* (prudent management) of one's environment and possessions as a prerequisite for divine safeguarding.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-161 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein who linked it up through a chain of narrators to God’s Prophet (MGB), “
The Honorable the Exalted God will not protect the following three people: those who reside in a ruined house; those who stand to pray on the road; and those who leave their vehicle unlocked.”
